title: Shapes and polarity: four molecules
promptMarkdown:
For each of $\ce{SF4}$, $\ce{XeF4}$, $\ce{NH3}$ and $\ce{SO3}$:

1. Give the valence-electron count, the AXE class, the electron-pair geometry, the molecular shape and the approximate bond angles (state whether the angles are compressed below the ideal and why).
2. Decide whether the molecule has a nonzero dipole moment and justify with the shape.
3. Explain why $\ce{SF4}$ exists but a molecule $\ce{OF4}$ with the same shape does not.
4. For $\ce{SO3}$, explain why the shape does not depend on which resonance structure you draw.
hintLadder: Count the regions of electron density around the central atom: each bonded atom is one region whatever the bond order, and each lone pair is one region.
Steric number 5 is a trigonal bipyramid, where lone pairs go equatorial; steric number 6 is an octahedron, where two lone pairs go opposite each other.
Draw the bond dipoles as arrows towards the more electronegative atom and ask whether they cancel by symmetry.
Which period is sulfur in, and which is oxygen in? What does that permit around the central atom?

deterministicChecks.description: claiming XeF4 or SO3 is polar, or SF4 nonpolar

criteria.criterion: SF4 AX4E (34 e⁻) trigonal bipyramidal / see-saw; XeF4 AX4E2 (36 e⁻) octahedral / square planar; NH3 AX3E (8 e⁻) tetrahedral / trigonal pyramidal; SO3 AX3 (24 e⁻) trigonal planar / trigonal planar.
Angles: SF4 slightly below 120° and 90° (and the axial F–S–F below 180°) because of the equatorial lone pair; XeF4 90°; NH3 below 109.5° (about 107°); SO3 120°.

criteria.criterion: S (period 3) can hold more than eight electrons, O (period 2) cannot, so OF4 would violate the octet; SO3's shape depends only on the three electron regions, common to all resonance forms.

checkExamples.label: correct answer
checkExamples.text: SF4: 34 valence electrons, AX4E, trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry, see-saw shape with the lone pair equatorial; the equatorial angle is a little under 120° and the axial under 180°; polar. XeF4: 36 electrons, AX4E2, octahedral, square planar, 90° angles; nonpolar because the four Xe–F dipoles cancel. NH3: 8 electrons, AX3E, tetrahedral, trigonal pyramidal, about 107°; polar. SO3: 24 electrons, AX3, trigonal planar, 120°; nonpolar by symmetry. SF4 exists because sulfur in period 3 can be hypervalent, while oxygen in period 2 cannot exceed an octet. SO3's three resonance structures all have three electron regions, so VSEPR gives the same shape for each.

checkExamples.label: tetrahedral guesses and polarity reversed
checkExamples.text: SF4 is tetrahedral. XeF4 is polar because of its lone pairs. SF4 is nonpolar.
